summary: Coast Guard light under the bluff at Prospect Point, Stanley Park: first shown in 1888, 1898 or about 1899 (sources differ); the present tower dates from 1948.

staffing.note: LighthouseFriends: the light was to be run from the signal station and the keeper's services ended.

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed. Reached on foot by the Stanley Park seawall from the park's parking areas.

events.note: LighthouseFriends: a light established on 1 October 1888. Disputed: Rowlett gives 1898 and the Vancouver marker puts the first lighthouse about eleven years after the 1888 grounding. See notes_for_editor.
Steamship Beaver ran aground just off the point. LighthouseFriends gives 25 July 1888; the marker says 1888.
Rowlett: station established 1898. Disputed; see the 1888 entry.
Steamship Princess Victoria struck the rocks while rounding Prospect Point on 17 July 1904; repaired and back in service 27 July.
An additional room was built onto the dwelling and the roof repaired, $242.85 (report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1906, printed 1907). LighthouseFriends dates the room to 1904.
The keeper also operated semaphore signal masts on a bluff about 150 ft above the light (LighthouseFriends).
Fixed white changed to occulting white, visible six seconds and eclipsed three seconds; fifth-order dioptric apparatus with petroleum vapour burner (report for the fiscal year ending 31 March 1911).
The signal station, not the light, was taken over from the Department of Marine and Fisheries and placed under the port authorities.
Light electrified and to be operated from the signal station; keeper's services ended (LighthouseFriends). The marker says the lighthouse was converted to electricity in 1926.
Present reinforced concrete tower built, at a cost of $7,712 (LighthouseFriends); 1948 (Rowlett).

keepers.name: John Grove
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends gives 1888 to 1926 ('Keepers: John Grove (1888 - 1926)'). The department's 1907 list reads 'Grove, John Prospect Point' (direct). The fiscal year ending 31 March 1910 table reads 'Jno. Grove July 7, 1898, 397.50'; the row is beside Prospect Point (checked on the page image, printed p.268, scan 270). The start year is still unresolved.

wrecks.outcome: Ran aground just off Prospect Point. Date from LighthouseFriends; the marker gives only the year.
Struck the rocks rounding Prospect Point into Vancouver harbour; starboard tail shaft bent, bracket twisted; repaired, back in service 27 July.

corrections.why: Spelling. The Coast Guard list and Rowlett both spell the point Prospect Point.
The present concrete tower is dated 1948 by Rowlett and by LighthouseFriends. Rowlett's 1898 is the station's establishment year, not the tower's.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The present tower is 1948 (Rowlett and LighthouseFriends agree). The first light is not settled: LighthouseFriends gives 1 October 1888; Rowlett gives 1898 as the station's establishment year; the Vancouver marker puts the first lighthouse about eleven years after the 1888 grounding. The story gives the disagreement and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-28. Every quote was found in its cached source on the first run (62 found, 0 missing). Corrected: (1) the $62 was the lowest wage Grove could pay a semaphore assistant, not what a man asked; (2) the light's characteristic is the Coast Guard's Iso R 2s; the one-second-on, one-second-off description is Rowlett's; (3) the marine agent offered to recommend that Grove keep his dwelling, not that he could stay; (4) fiscal years now follow the reports (1907 report = year ended 30 June 1906; 1910 table = year ending 31 March 1910; the 1911 change = year ending 31 March 1911); (5) the 1888 grounding is 'just off the point' (marker), and the 'Jno. Grove' date is marked as matched by row. FIRST LIGHT IS UNSETTLED: 1 October 1888 (LighthouseFriends, no primary cited); 'station established 1898' (Rowlett); 'eleven years' after the 1888 grounding, about 1899 (the marker). The Department reports for 1888-1899 are not in the corpus, so this is not checked against a primary source. JNO. GROVE (matched by row, checked on the Internet Archive page image): in the 1910 table the 'Jno. Grove, July 7, 1898, 397.50' row sits beside 'Prospect Point'; the row beside 'Portlock Point' carries W. J. Gillespie, who is listed at Portlock Point in the 1907 list. The 1915 list also has 'J. Grove' at Prospect Point (not used). THE ROOM: LighthouseFriends dates the added room to 1904; the 1907 report (year ended 30 June 1906) records it among repairs; both kept. BEAVER DATE: 25 July 1888 is LighthouseFriends only; the marker gives the year. PRESENT TOWER (1948): LighthouseFriends and Rowlett only; the corpus ends in 1924. ACCESS: grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends, Rowlett). Capilano light (1908) is context only. Photos: none new. Confidence medium: the 1888-1898 question is the main open item.
